title: Certificates of Deposit: Grace Add-Ons and the Account Named for Interest Payouts
content:
Money placed during grace into any of the bank's Certificates of Deposit becomes capital on which the renewed term's interest will be credited and, where the owner has chosen payouts, paid out. The bank therefore accepts grace money only into a certificate whose interest setting points somewhere that interest can actually reach. This page states that condition.

## Rule

On a tier that accepts add-ons in grace, grace money is taken (each deposit at or above the tier's grace minimum, all of the period's grace deposits together within its grace maximum) only for as long as the interest disposition on the certificate points at no payout account that has been closed.

Whether it points at one is read as follows:

- an interest disposition of compounding names no payout account at all, so it never blocks grace money;
- an interest disposition paying to checking is judged on the status of the payout account among the owner's checking accounts;
- an interest disposition paying to savings is judged on the status of the payout account among the owner's savings accounts.

A status of closed means the disposition points at a closed payout account, and for as long as it does, no top-up is written, whatever the size of the gap.

## Input, judgement, outcome (hypothetical)

| Interest disposition | Status of the payout account on file | Grace money accepted? |
|---|---|---|
| Compounding | (not relevant) | Yes, as far as this rule goes |
| Paid to savings | savings account active | Yes, as far as this rule goes |
| Paid to savings | savings account closed | No |
| Paid to checking | checking account closed | No |
| Paid to checking | checking account active | Yes, as far as this rule goes |
